meta.title: openCMA | Vehicle Diagnostics for Volvo & Polestar
meta.description: Source-available vehicle diagnostics, battery health and live telemetry for supported Volvo and Polestar vehicles over DoIP and UDS. Local, private and for personal use.

common.sampleData: Fixed sample data, not a vehicle reading
common.representative: Representative interface with sample values. Not a live vehicle reading.

hero.title: Read your Volvo or Polestar the way a workshop does.
hero.lead: Connect to a supported Volvo or Polestar over Ethernet. Read battery health, ECU faults and live telemetry. No cloud, no subscription.

connection.title: A passive cable is the whole interface.
connection.lead: A passive ENET cable and any Ethernet interface are enough to reach a supported vehicle. Select a part of the chain to see what it does.

features.title: Everything the vehicle will tell you, over one connection.
features.lead: The battery, every ECU, faults, live data and service routines, read over one connection. No mode switching between tools.
features.batteryBody: State of health and charge, pack voltage, cell-group spread, min, max and delta, and pack temperature. The percentage your dashboard shows, and the numbers behind it.
features.scanBody: openCMA discovers ECUs over DoIP, identifies which speak UDS, and reads the identification, hardware and software data from each.
features.faultBody: openCMA reads DTCs with their status: active now, pending, stored or historical. If the ECU saved a snapshot when the fault set, you get that too.
features.liveBody: Pack voltage and current, battery and inverter temperature, motor torque, the 12 V system. Sampled on a loop and plotted on fixed axes.
features.serviceBody: EPB service mode, 12 V battery adaptation, service reminder reset, HVAC damper calibration and selected UDS routines, where the platform supports them.
features.evidenceTitle: Before and after, side by side
features.evidenceBody: Export a session to JSON or CSV, do the repair, scan again, and compare the two exports.
features.readOnlyNote: Read-only diagnostics stay read-only. Write-capable routines are kept separate and stay disabled until you enable them for the session.

platforms.title: CMA-first, with expanding DoIP support.
platforms.lead: Polestar 2 and the CMA Volvos are the tested platforms. SPA hybrids and newer SEA and SPA2 cars connect, but openCMA cannot fully decode what they send yet. Reaching a car is not the same as supporting it.
platforms.disclaimer: Compatibility is not a claim of manufacturer support. openCMA is an independent project and is not affiliated with Volvo Cars, Polestar or Geely.

blurbs.CMA: Compact Modular Architecture. The tested platform: Polestar 2 and the smaller electric Volvos.
blurbs.SPA: Scalable Product Architecture. First-generation Recharge plug-in hybrids. openCMA recognises the platform but is still mapping it.
blurbs.SEA: Sustainable Experience Architecture. Newer BEVs including Zeekr. Platform mapping under verification.
blurbs.SPA2: Second-generation SPA. Different gateway and security model. Under investigation.

statusNotes.supported: Verified runtime implementation. Battery, DTC, ECU identification and live data are exercised regularly.
statusNotes.partial: Some functions are implemented and verified. Others are not yet covered on this vehicle.
statusNotes.testing: The code is there, but it has not been checked against a known-good reference yet.
statusNotes.wip: Under active development. It connects, but the decoding is incomplete and changes from release to release.
statusNotes.research: Architecture is being investigated. Not usable for diagnostics.
statusNotes.planned: On the roadmap. No implementation yet.

protocolStack.title: Built on automotive standards.
protocolStack.lead: openCMA talks to the car's diagnostic network with the same protocols a dealer tool uses. Nothing in between is a proprietary cloud service.
protocolStack.paragraph: A session starts with UDP discovery on port 13400, opens a TCP channel, activates routing, then exchanges UDS requests: read by identifier, read DTC information, session control and routine control.

privacy.title: Your vehicle data stays with you.
privacy.lead: openCMA talks to the vehicle and writes diagnostic data to your disk. There is no backend and no subscription, and nothing about your car is uploaded or sold. The VIN is stripped from logs and exports that don't need it.
privacy.directLink: Direct link. Nothing else in the path.

hardware.title: The adapter is just a cable.
hardware.lead: A passive ENET cable wires the vehicle's OBD-II pins to an RJ45 plug. From there it's ordinary Ethernet to your computer.

notWanted.elm: No ELM327 or generic OBD dongle
notWanted.j2534: No J2534 pass-through interface for standard DoIP
notWanted.driver: No driver install for a passive ENET cable

safety.title: Read-only by default. Writes are gated.
safety.lead: openCMA mostly reads. The operations that change the vehicle are kept separate and stay off until you turn on write access for the session.
safety.highVoltageBody: Electric vehicles carry hazardous high-voltage systems. Reading data over a cable does not make it safe to work on them, and openCMA is not a substitute for the manufacturer's service procedures.

home.q: Do I need a special diagnostic tool or dongle?
home.a: No. A passive ENET cable (OBD-II to RJ45) and any Ethernet interface on your computer are enough for DoIP on supported vehicles. None of the usual OBD dongles are involved.

home.q: Does openCMA send any data anywhere?
home.a: No. It communicates only with the vehicle and writes results to your disk. There is no account, no backend, no analytics and no telemetry. The VIN is kept out of logs and exports unless something needs it.

Polestar 2 and the CMA-platform Volvos (XC40/EX40, C40/EC40) are the tested platforms. Newer SEA and SPA2 cars connect over DoIP but their ECU maps and battery decoding are still being verified and are marked Experimental or Research.

Standard use is read-only. Operations that change the vehicle (clearing DTCs, service routines, adaptations) are separated in the interface and disabled unless you enable write access for that session. High-voltage service still requires the manufacturer's procedures.

home.q: Is this an official Volvo or Polestar tool?
home.a: No. openCMA is an independent project. It is not affiliated with, maintained by or authorised by Volvo Cars, Polestar or Geely. The source is available to read. It is provided for personal, non-commercial use.

home.q: What can I do with the battery data?
home.a: Read state of health and charge, pack voltage, per-cell-group potentials for all 108 positions on CMA, min/max/delta and pack temperature, and export a session to compare before and after a repair.

compat.q: Does openCMA work with any Volvo or Polestar?
compat.a: No. openCMA is CMA-first. Polestar 2 and the CMA Volvos (XC40/EX40, C40/EC40) are the tested platforms. SPA plug-in hybrids and newer SEA and SPA2 cars connect over DoIP, but their decoding is still being worked out and is marked WIP or Research.

compat.q: What is the difference between platform compatibility and support?
compat.a: Platform compatibility means openCMA can reach the vehicle over DoIP. Support means the diagnostic functions are implemented and verified against known-good references. Being reachable does not make the data trustworthy, which is why WIP and Research platforms are labelled separately.

compat.q: My car is listed as WIP or Research. Can I use it?
compat.a: You can connect and, on some, read identification data. Do not rely on battery figures or fault interpretation, and do not run service routines. WIP and Research mean the decoding is not verified.

compat.q: Is this endorsed by Volvo or Polestar?
compat.a: No. openCMA is an independent project, not affiliated with, maintained by or authorised by Volvo Cars, Polestar or Geely. Manufacturer names are used only to describe compatibility.

pages.featuresLead: Four areas of coverage, read over the same connection. Standard diagnostics stay read-only; write-capable functions are separated and gated.
pages.batteryHealthTitle: The percentage, and the numbers behind it.
pages.batteryHealthLead: openCMA reads high-voltage battery data reported by the vehicle: state of health and charge, pack voltage, cell-group distribution, imbalance and temperature.
pages.vehicleDiagnosticsTitle: Every ECU on the network, not just the one with the light on.
pages.vehicleDiagnosticsLead: openCMA discovers the vehicle ECUs over DoIP, identifies which speak UDS, and reads fault and identification data from each.
pages.liveDataTitle: Engineering telemetry on a polling loop.
pages.liveDataLead: openCMA polls data identifiers on a loop and plots them like instrumentation software: fixed axes, thin traces, no decoration.
pages.serviceFunctionsTitle: The operations that change the vehicle stay separate.
pages.serviceFunctionsLead: Where the platform supports them, openCMA can run service routines and adaptations. These are not part of ordinary diagnostics and are disabled until you enable write access.
pages.vehiclesTitle: CMA-first, with expanding DoIP platform support.
pages.vehiclesLead: Select a platform and a vehicle to see exactly which functions are verified. Each status label reflects what has been checked on that car, not just the platform it is built on.
pages.downloadLead: Native builds for each desktop platform. Nothing installs automatically and nothing phones home.
pages.safetyTitle: What is safe, and what is not.
pages.safetyLead: Diagnostic software can read a great deal and change a few things. openCMA is built so you always know which is which.
pages.privacyLead: openCMA has no backend and no account system. It talks to the vehicle and writes to your disk. That is the whole data path.
pages.aboutTitle: A project for people who want to understand their vehicles.
pages.aboutLead: openCMA started as a way to read CMA battery data without a dealer subscription. It grew into a general DoIP and UDS diagnostic tool.
